findings.title: Team permission check uses AND of isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both an admin *and* the owner. Despite the variable name, a team ADMIN who is not the owner will be denied, and the combined condition is effectively "is owner" only. This should be an OR (or a single role check). Consequence: team admins who are legitimately allowed to manage team bookings cannot add guests. It also issues two extra DB queries with `teamId ?? 0` for personal bookings.

findings.title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive, allowing bypass and duplicate attendees
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lower-cased, but the incoming `guest` string is never normalized, so `Blocked@Example.com` passes the blacklist filter while `blocked@example.com` would be blocked. The duplicate check `attendee.email === guest` is likewise case-sensitive, so an existing attendee can be added again with different casing, creating a second attendee row and duplicate emails for the same person. Normalize (trim + lowercase) guest emails before both checks and before persisting.

findings.title: Input guest list is not de-duplicated server-side
findings.body: The filter only removes guests that already exist as attendees or are blacklisted; it does not de-duplicate the `guests` array itself. The client dialog enforces uniqueness, but the tRPC endpoint is callable directly, so `guests: ["a@x.com", "a@x.com"]` creates two attendee rows for the same email on the booking, which then receive duplicate emails and show up twice in the booking UI and calendar event. De-duplicate (e.g. via a Set) before `createMany`.

findings.title: Calendar/video update uses the acting user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
findings.body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` build the EventManager from the session user, while `evt.destinationCalendar` is derived from the booking's organizer/destination calendar. When a team admin/owner or an attendee (both allowed by the permission check above) adds guests, the handler will try to update the organizer's calendar event with the wrong account's credentials, so `updateCalendarAttendees` silently fails or targets an unrelated calendar and the external event is never updated with the new guests. The organizer's credentials (`booking.user.credentials`, already fetched) should be used.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw input instead of the actually-added guests
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the unfiltered input array. In `email-manager.sendAddGuestsEmails`, membership in this array decides whether an attendee gets a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (new-booking style) or the `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` notification. Any email the caller submitted that was filtered out because it is already an attendee therefore receives a brand-new "booking confirmed" email instead of the "guests added" notification. `uniqueGuests` should be passed instead.

findings.title: Email failure is swallowed without logging the error
findings.body: `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` discards `err` entirely and uses `console.log` rather than the project `logger`. If sending fails (bad SMTP config, template error) there is no stack trace or context (bookingId, guests) to debug with, and the mutation still reports success to the user.

findings.title: No validation of booking status; guests can be added to cancelled, rejected or past bookings
findings.body: The handler only checks existence and permissions. It never inspects `booking.status` or `booking.endTime`, so a caller can add guests to a CANCELLED/REJECTED booking or to one that already ended; in each case new attendee rows are created and "guests added" emails with a CONFIRMED ICS (`status: "CONFIRMED"`, `method: "REQUEST"`) are sent out, which can re-create a cancelled event on recipients' calendars. The UI also surfaces this action for past bookings (editBookingActions is rendered for past/confirmed bookings), so the server must reject these cases.

findings.title: Attendees are created without seat references for seated event types
findings.body: For event types with `seatsPerTimeSlot`, every attendee is normally paired with a `BookingSeat` record (seatsReferences). This handler inserts attendees directly via `attendees.createMany` with no seat reference and without checking remaining seat capacity, so seated bookings end up with attendees that have no seat uid. Those guests cannot cancel/reschedule via the seat flow and the booking can exceed its configured seat count.

findings.title: No upper bound on the number of guests accepted
findings.body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()` constraint. Any authenticated user who is an attendee or organizer of a booking can submit an arbitrarily long list of arbitrary email addresses; each one is persisted as an attendee and receives an email from the Cal.com mail server. This is a mail-amplification/spam vector and an unbounded DB write. Add a reasonable maximum (and a minimum of 1) to the schema.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings
findings.body: Every other sender in this file (e.g. `sendLocationChangeEmails`) takes an `eventTypeMetadata` argument and guards with `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`. `sendAddGuestsEmails` accepts no metadata and unconditionally emails the organizer, all team members and all attendees, so event types configured with standard host/attendee emails disabled will still send mail, breaking that setting.

findings.title: Component inside packages/ui imports from its own barrel (@calcom/ui), creating a circular dependency
findings.body: `import { Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip } from "@calcom/ui";` imports the package's own entry point (`packages/ui/index.tsx`), which in turn re-exports this very module via `./form/MultiEmailLazy`. Sibling components in this folder import their dependencies by relative path for this reason. The cycle can produce undefined imports at runtime (especially combined with the `next/dynamic` lazy wrapper) and pulls the whole UI barrel into the lazily-loaded chunk, defeating the purpose of `MultiEmailLazy`. Use relative imports (`../components/button`, `../components/form`, etc.).

findings.title: Hardcoded English tooltip text in shared UI component
findings.body: `<Tooltip content="Remove email">` uses a hardcoded English string in a shared, user-facing component while the rest of the component uses `t(...)`. Non-English users will see untranslated text; the string should come from the locale files.

findings.title: Error toast exposes raw tRPC code and the fallback message is dead code
findings.body: `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`` is always a non-empty string, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` can never fall back; when `err.data` is missing the user sees `undefined: ...`. The toast also surfaces an internal error code plus an un-translated server message key to end users. Prefer translating the known message keys and falling back to `t("unable_to_add_guests")` when the key is unknown.

findings.title: Validation error state is never cleared except via Cancel
findings.body: `setIsInvalidEmail(true)` is only reset in the Cancel button handler. If the user fixes the invalid/duplicate emails and submits successfully, or closes the dialog with the X/overlay and reopens it, the red "Emails must be unique and valid" message remains visible. Reset the flag at the start of `handleAdd` and when the dialog opens/closes.

findings.title: New mutation with non-trivial authorization logic has no tests
findings.body: `addGuestsHandler` introduces an authorization matrix (organizer / team admin-owner / attendee), blacklist filtering, duplicate filtering, attendee persistence, calendar update and email dispatch, but the PR adds no unit or integration tests. Given the permission bug (AND instead of OR), the case-sensitivity bypass and the credential mix-up noted elsewhere in this review, tests covering at least the authorization branches and the filtering of duplicates/blacklisted emails are needed before merge.
